about: The asset table (package A, 26 Nov 2026; replaces catalogue/distances.json): what a kind of development is like, apart from who's asking (the profile). For each asset type: its names as people say them; the screening scale its size picks (local, regional or global: which of each check's reaches in catalogue/checks.json applies); the footprint radius used when the site is only a point; where it extends a check's reach, with the reason and the source; and the effects it sends out. A check owns its default reach; an asset row only extends it, never cuts it; the person's own distances override both. Protection distances (the developable area's buffers) are in protection below where a source gives one (package D, 27 Nov); elsewhere the skill's own first cuts stand. Nothing is fetched beyond 50 km. Read by js/reach.js; tested in test/reach.test.mjs.

fields.names: how people say it, lower case; read from the person's words in code (js/assetwords.js, package E). general.planned lists what has no row (housing, a warehouse): read the same way, screened on the general defaults with its label. counts: words after a number that also name it (a 200-home scheme). A planned label may carry extends of its own (package D, 28 Nov): its scale and footprint stay the general defaults
fields.scale: the screening scale for this asset in this setting, with why. by_size rules apply in order, each overriding what it names: below_mw, mw (at least), area_km2 (at least), below_km2. A rule's keeps names a scale whose checks the run also keeps, each check taking the further of its two reaches
fields.footprint_km: the radius of the circle used when the site is only a point: the footprint's own width, which belongs to the place, not a search distance
fields.extends: checks (by id) or topics whose reach this asset extends, to to_km, or by_tip_height ([[up_to_m, km], …, [null, km]]) when the tip height is given. Each has why, source and, from package D (28 Nov), basis (reg, gov, prof, plan, case, as in protection). countries: where the extension applies, by the world outlines' names; none means everywhere. Never shortens a check
fields.effects: how its effects travel (sight, flight, water, ground, road, sound), each with a source; nothing reads it yet (package E)
fields.pair: the row to use instead when the place is in the other setting (wind farm words for a site at sea read as offshore wind)

protection.about: Protection distances (package D, researched 26 Nov 2026 in claude/research-asset-reaches.md §2, reviewed by Rob 26 and 27 Nov): the developable area's buffers where a rule, guidance or a professional body gives one. A row names the deduction it sets (by the developable area skill's id), the assets it's for (all, or a list), and where it applies: countries by the world outlines' names, and in, UK nations or states, matched on real outlines (invariant 2). A row whose state Tobler can't decide (no outlines for that country yet) isn't applied, and the card says so. Where no row applies, the skill's own buffer stands, marked as a first cut. The person's own distance beats both. Metric in the record; as_published keeps the source's words. basis: reg (law), gov (government guidance), prof (professional body), plan, case; secondary: the figure is from a secondary source until the primary is read. Read by js/developable.js.

rows.as_published: a buffer of at least 15 m, more where effects reach further
rows.reason: Irreplaceable habitat. Natural England and the Forestry Commission's standing advice is a buffer of at least 15 m, more where effects such as air pollution reach further.

source.title: Ancient woodland, ancient trees and veteran trees: advice for making planning decisions

rows.varies: A 50 m minimum was proposed in 2021 and not adopted; objectors ask for more case by case

rows.as_published: 8 m from a main river (16 m if tidal)
rows.reason: Work within 8 m of a main river (16 m if tidal) needs a flood risk activity permit. OpenStreetMap doesn't say which streams are main rivers or tidal, so every watercourse gets 8 m. A permit trigger, not a ban.

source.title: Flood risk activities: environmental permits; Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016, Schedule 25

rows.as_published: 30 m initial minimum separation to occupied buildings (was 25 m)
rows.reason: The fire and rescue services' initial minimum separation between battery units and occupied buildings. It's for fire, not noise: noise is assessed site by site. Residential land, gardens included.

source.title: Grid scale battery energy storage system planning: guidance for fire and rescue services (as reported)

rows.as_published: 5 m either side of the centreline (4 m for gas at 16 to 40 bar)
rows.reason: The strip either side of a pipeline where building is restricted by law (Bkl §5.1.2.3). The pipeline's own risk distances come on top and aren't measured here.

rows.as_published: 1 km from a dwelling unless the owner consents in writing
rows.reason: Victoria's planning rule: no turbine within 1 km of a dwelling without the owner's written consent.

source.title: Planning guidelines for development of wind energy facilities (clause 52.32)
source.publisher: Victoria Department of Transport and Planning

rows.as_published: 1,500 m from sensitive land uses on non-host lots, or a deed
rows.reason: Queensland's state code: turbines at least 1,500 m from sensitive land uses on lots not hosting the wind farm, unless there's a deed of agreement.

source.title: SDAP State code 23: wind farm development, AO10.1

rows.as_published: 1,000 ft from a distribution centre with more than 100 trucks a day
rows.reason: California's air quality advice: keep homes, schools and care 1,000 ft from a distribution centre with more than 100 trucks a day (or 40 refrigerated trucks). Advisory, not a rule.

source.title: Air Quality and Land Use Handbook (2005), Table 1-1
